name: How do you know if a design-build company is truly full-service?

mainEntity.name: What signs show that a company can actually handle design, permits, and construction in-house or through one coordinated team?
mainEntity.text: What signs show that a company can actually handle design, permits, and construction in-house or through one coordinated team?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full-service design-build company should be able to explain its workflow from the first consultation to final walkthrough. That includes who develops the design, who prepares estimates, who submits permits, who manages trades, and who answers questions during construction. The company should also be able to show completed projects that look similar to yours and explain how it coordinated the work. If design, pricing, and construction are passed around with little structure, the process may not be truly integrated. Homeowners should also ask whether the team uses in-house staff, long-term consultants, or outside subcontractors for key tasks. The goal is not that every person must be on payroll, but that the homeowner gets a coordinated experience with clear accountability. Specific answers are a much better sign than marketing language.
acceptedAnswer.description: A truly full-service design-build company can show how it manages design, estimating, permits, project management, and construction under one process. It should have clear examples, a defined workflow, and a single point of contact. If the company cannot explain who does what, it may not be fully integrated.
